3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

346	CASE OD2-HO-INCOMPLETE-1 (INCOMPLETE, technical): Chiller-plant electricity up 15% with flat production
347	Setting: Velmora Plastics' Østrand site extrudes plastic profiles and moulds small components. A central plant of three 1,400 kW water-cooled centrifugal chillers (CH-1 to CH-3), two cooling towers and variable-speed secondary pumps supplies 7 °C process chilled water to the extrusion lines and other process users. The chiller plant's electricity (chillers, pumps, tower fans) is submetered at MCC-4. The site energy coordinator has escalated a sustained year-on-year rise in chiller-plant electricity that nobody on site can account for.
348	Presenting request: The site director asks: why has chiller-plant electricity risen about 15% year on year when production is flat, and should she approve the chiller service vendor's €38,400 condenser cleaning now? She wants a recommendation this week.

Change vs same month of prior year: Jan +1%, Feb 0%, Mar +2%, Apr +4%, May +9%, Jun +14%, Jul +17%, Aug +18%, Sep +19%, Oct +20%. Site utility revenue meter, Apr–Oct: 3,520 → 3,738 MWh (+218 MWh). Site total minus MCC-4: 2,108 → 2,110 MWh. Weather, Tarnby airfield station: cooling degree-days Apr–Oct 2% lower in 2026 than 2025; mean daily wet-bulb 0.3 K lower. Extra chiller-plant cost for the period at current tariff ≈ €41,000.
351	E2 [stage S1] BMS 'Plant Efficiency' dashboard export, pulled 4 Nov 2026 (telemetry): Plant efficiency = MCC-4 kWe ÷ kW of cooling delivered. Apr–Oct 2025 average 0.182 (monthly values 0.180–0.184). Apr–Oct 2026 average 0.209 (+15%). Monthly 2026: Apr 0.190, May 0.199, Jun 0.208, Jul 0.214, Aug 0.215, Sep 0.217, Oct 0.219. Cooling delivered, period average: 2025 1,510 kW; 2026 1,517 kW (+0.5%). Dashboard footnote: 'Cooling delivered = chilled-water header flow (FT-201) × (return temperature TT-202 − supply temperature TT-201) × fluid constant. Values shown as recorded.'
352	E3 [stage S1] Kestrel Cooling Services field service report, visit of 18 Sep 2026 (vendor-account): Visit to CH-1 at customer request. Readings at 92% load: leaving condenser water 29.4 °C, condensing temperature 31.3 °C, approach 1.9 K. The 2019 start-up sheet records an approach of 1.1 K; load at start-up is not recorded on our copy. Approach normally rises with load, but in our experience a 0.8 K increase points to tube fouling, likely following the change of water-treatment contractor in January. Tubes last brushed February 2025. CH-2 and CH-3 not measured this visit. Recommendation: mechanical brushing of all three condensers, €38,400, plus enrolment in our Performance Assurance contract (€14,200/yr) to prevent recurrence.
353	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Tomas Reiner, production manager, 5 Nov 2026 (manager-account): Shipped tonnage Apr–Oct is within 1% of last year and the product mix hasn't moved. We haven't added anything to the chilled-water loop. The moulding cell moved from Building C to the new Building F between April and June, but that was like-for-like, same presses, and Building F was designed with its own cooling. Please don't touch the water temperature: extrusion and the moulds need 7 °C supply. When it drifted to 8.5 °C for a week in 2024 we had a scrap spike on lines 2 and 3 and missed two customer deliveries.
